events.title: Transformer architecture introduced
events.note: Vaswani et al. replaced recurrence with self-attention, enabling highly parallel training; nearly every later LLM builds on this architecture.

events.title: RL from human preferences
events.note: Showed agents could learn complex goals from human comparisons of their behavior, the preference-learning idea later adapted to fine-tune language models with RLHF.

events.title: GPT-1 introduced
events.note: OpenAI paired a Transformer with unsupervised pre-training on unlabeled text followed by task-specific fine-tuning, the basic recipe that later GPT models scaled up.

events.title: BERT released
events.note: Bidirectional pre-training with masked-word prediction set new state-of-the-art results on eleven NLP tasks, popularizing fine-tuned encoder models for language understanding.

events.title: GPT-2 announced with staged release
events.note: OpenAI's 1.5B-parameter model wrote fluent passages of text, and the company held back the full weights over misuse concerns, releasing larger versions in stages.

events.title: T5 text-to-text framework
events.note: T5 cast every NLP task as text in, text out, systematically compared pre-training choices, and released the C4 web corpus with its models.

events.title: Neural scaling laws published
events.note: Kaplan et al. found language-model loss falls predictably as a power law in parameters, data and compute, giving labs a basis for planning larger training runs.

events.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
events.note: Paired a text generator with a neural retriever over a document index, an approach now widely used to ground chatbots in current or private documents.

events.title: GPT-3 introduced
events.note: At 175B parameters, GPT-3 could perform many tasks from a few examples in the prompt, popularizing in-context learning as an alternative to fine-tuning.

events.title: Switch Transformers scale sparse MoE
events.note: Routing each token to a single expert let Google train trillion-parameter sparse models efficiently, an early proof point for the mixture-of-experts designs common in later LLMs.

events.title: LoRA fine-tuning method
events.note: Freezing pretrained weights and training small low-rank update matrices cut trainable parameters by 10,000x on GPT-3, making custom fine-tunes far cheaper.

events.title: Chain-of-thought prompting
events.note: Wei et al. showed that prompting large models to write out intermediate steps markedly improved arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning, an idea later built into reasoning models.

events.title: InstructGPT applies RLHF to LLMs
events.note: Fine-tuning GPT-3 on human demonstrations and preference rankings produced a 1.3B model that labelers preferred over the 175B original, a method ChatGPT later adopted.

events.title: Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling
events.note: DeepMind found large models were significantly undertrained; its 70B Chinchilla, trained on more data, outperformed far larger models and influenced how labs balance size against data.

events.title: BLOOM open multilingual model
events.note: Built by the BigScience research collaboration, the 176B-parameter model covered 46 natural and 13 programming languages and was openly released under a Responsible AI License.

events.title: ChatGPT launched
events.note: A free research preview of a GPT-3.5-based assistant tuned with RLHF brought conversational AI to a mass audience; rival assistants from Google and Anthropic followed within months.

events.title: Constitutional AI
events.note: Anthropic trained a harmless assistant using AI feedback guided by a written set of principles, reducing reliance on human labels for safety training.

events.title: Microsoft expands OpenAI partnership
events.note: A third phase of the partnership brought a multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment and more Azure supercomputing, showing how closely frontier labs depend on hyperscale cloud compute.

events.title: Google announces Bard
events.note: Google opened its experimental Bard chatbot to trusted testers ahead of a public release and previewed AI features for Search; Bard was later renamed Gemini.

events.title: Meta releases LLaMA
events.note: Meta shared 7B to 65B models with approved researchers under a noncommercial license and reported that its 13B version outperformed 175B GPT-3 on most benchmarks.

events.title: GPT-4 released
events.note: OpenAI's multimodal model accepted images and text and scored around the top 10% on a simulated bar exam, versus the bottom 10% for GPT-3.5.

events.title: Anthropic launches Claude
events.note: After a closed alpha with partners such as Notion and Quora, Anthropic opened its Claude assistant more widely through a chat interface and API.

events.title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
events.note: Researchers showed models can be aligned to human preferences with a simple classification-style loss, skipping the separate reward model and RL loop that RLHF requires.

events.title: Llama 2 released for commercial use
events.note: Meta, with Microsoft as a launch partner, made Llama 2 weights free for research and commercial use, giving companies a capable model they could self-host.

events.title: Mistral 7B released
events.note: A 7.3B-parameter Apache 2.0 model that Mistral reported beat Llama 2 13B on all its benchmarks, showing small open models could outperform larger ones.

events.title: Bletchley Declaration on AI safety
events.note: At the first AI Safety Summit, 28 countries and the EU, including the US and China, agreed that frontier AI risks require international cooperation.

events.title: Gemini 1.0 launched
events.note: Google's first Gemini models came in Ultra, Pro and Nano sizes and were built from the start to handle text, images, audio, code and video.

events.title: Mixtral 8x7B released
events.note: A sparse mixture-of-experts model using about 12.9B of its 46.7B parameters per token, bringing MoE efficiency to an openly licensed Apache 2.0 model.

events.title: Phi-2 small language model
events.note: Microsoft's 2.7B-parameter model matched or beat models up to 25 times its size on complex benchmarks, strengthening the case for small language models.

events.title: Gemini 1.5 previews 1M-token context
events.note: Gemini 1.5 Pro neared Gemini 1.0 Ultra's performance and let selected developers test a 1M-token context window, about eight times its standard 128K limit.

events.title: Claude 3 model family
events.note: Anthropic introduced Haiku, Sonnet and Opus as a three-tier family with 200K-token context, giving developers a clear speed, cost and capability trade-off.

events.title: Grok-1 weights released
events.note: xAI published Grok-1's raw 314B-parameter mixture-of-experts base checkpoint under Apache 2.0, giving researchers a very large, permissively licensed model to study and adapt.

events.title: GPT-4o released
events.note: OpenAI's omni model took any mix of text, audio, image and video input and could reply to speech in about the time a person takes in conversation.

events.title: Llama 3.1 405B released
events.note: Meta's 405B-parameter model with 128K context was the largest Llama yet, and Meta presented it as the first openly available model on par with leading frontier systems.

events.title: EU AI Act enters into force
events.note: The EU's risk-based AI law took effect, with bans, general-purpose model duties and high-risk requirements set to phase in over the following years.

events.title: OpenAI o1-preview
events.note: The first of OpenAI's o-series reasoning models spent extra time thinking before answering, showing that inference-time reasoning could lift math, science and coding results.

events.title: Claude computer use beta
events.note: An upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet could operate a computer by viewing screenshots, moving the cursor, clicking and typing, an early public step toward computer-using agents.

events.title: Model Context Protocol released
events.note: Anthropic open-sourced a protocol for linking AI assistants to tools and data, letting developers build a connector once and reuse it across compatible apps.

events.title: DeepSeek-V3 released
events.note: DeepSeek's 671B-parameter MoE model (37B active) reported results comparable to leading closed models from a full training run of 2.788M H800 GPU hours.

events.title: DeepSeek-R1 released
events.note: DeepSeek's MIT-licensed model, trained largely with reinforcement learning, reported reasoning performance on par with OpenAI o1 and arrived with six smaller distilled versions.

events.title: EU AI Act bans take effect
events.note: Prohibitions on unacceptable-risk practices such as social scoring began applying, along with AI literacy duties, the Act's first binding obligations.

events.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code
events.note: Anthropic's first hybrid reasoning model let users switch on extended thinking, and debuted alongside Claude Code, a terminal tool for delegating coding tasks.

events.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro introduced
events.note: Google's reasoning-focused Pro model debuted at the top of the LMArena leaderboard and led several math, science and coding benchmarks.

events.title: Llama 4 Scout and Maverick
events.note: Meta's first mixture-of-experts Llamas were natively multimodal, with Scout advertising a 10M-token context window; the larger Behemoth was previewed but not released.

events.title: Qwen3 family released
events.note: Alibaba released eight Apache 2.0 models, from 0.6B dense to a 235B mixture-of-experts flagship, each able to switch between step-by-step thinking and fast replies.

events.title: Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4
events.note: Anthropic pitched Opus 4 as the world's best coding model, citing 72.5% on SWE-bench, and made Claude Code generally available with beta IDE extensions.

events.title: Kimi K2 open weights
events.note: Moonshot AI released a 1-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 32B active parameters under a modified MIT license, aimed at agentic tasks such as tool use.

events.title: Grok 4 released
events.note: Trained with large-scale reinforcement learning on xAI's Colossus cluster, Grok 4 shipped with native tool use and a multi-agent Heavy tier aimed at hard reasoning tasks.

events.title: EU AI Act rules for general-purpose AI apply
events.note: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models, including LLMs, began applying, with stricter duties for the most capable models deemed to pose systemic risk.

events.title: OpenAI releases gpt-oss
events.note: OpenAI's first open-weight language models since GPT-2: Apache 2.0 reasoning models sized to run on a single 80 GB GPU (120b) or within 16 GB of memory (20b).

events.title: GPT-5 released
events.note: GPT-5 combined a fast model and a deeper reasoning model behind an automatic router and reached ChatGPT's free tier, putting reasoning in front of mainstream users.

events.title: Gemini 3 Pro released
events.note: Google's new flagship topped LMArena with a 1501 Elo score and launched alongside Antigravity, an agentic development platform, across Search, the Gemini app and developer tools.

events.title: Mistral 3 family released
events.note: Mistral Large 3, a 675B-parameter MoE with 41B active, and three small Ministral 3 models arrived under Apache 2.0, all with image understanding.

events.title: Claude Opus 4.6 released
events.note: Anthropic's first Opus-class model with a 1M-token context window (in beta) added 128K-token outputs and agent teams in Claude Code for longer autonomous work.

events.title: GPT-5.4 released
events.note: GPT-5.4 merged GPT-5.3-Codex's coding strengths with built-in computer use, scoring 75.0% on OSWorld-Verified against a human baseline of 72.4% cited by OpenAI.

events.title: Gemma 4 open models
events.note: Google DeepMind's open models, from phone-scale E2B to a 31B dense model and a 26B mixture-of-experts, shipped under Apache 2.0 rather than earlier Gemma's custom terms.

events.title: Claude Mythos Preview and Project Glasswing
events.note: Anthropic withheld Claude Mythos Preview from general release over its skill at finding and exploiting software flaws, limiting it to defensive partners such as AWS, Apple and Microsoft.

events.title: GPT-5.5 released
events.note: OpenAI positioned GPT-5.5 for long, multi-step computer work, reporting leading scores on agentic benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench 2.0 (82.7%) and OSWorld-Verified (78.7%).

events.title: DeepSeek V4 preview released
events.note: DeepSeek open-sourced a 1.6-trillion-parameter Pro model and a 284B Flash model, both with 1M-token context, making million-token windows the default across its services.

events.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash released
events.note: Unveiled at Google I/O, Gemini 3.5 Flash opened Google's 3.5 generation and was generally available in the Gemini API on day one; a larger 3.5 Pro was promised later.

events.title: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 released
events.note: Anthropic made a Mythos-class model generally available as Fable 5, routing some cyber, bio and distillation queries to Opus 4.8, while the less-restricted Mythos 5 went to vetted partners.

events.title: EU AI Act high-risk deadlines delayed
events.note: The Digital Omnibus amendments pushed high-risk AI obligations to December 2027 and August 2028, days before the Act's general application date of August 2, 2026.

events.title: Qwen3.8 open weights released
events.note: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 open-weight releases included a 27B Apache 2.0 model and a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts flagship (95B active) under a separate custom license.

events.title: GPT-6 Astra released
events.note: OpenAI opened its GPT-6 generation with Astra, which it said met its 'Critical' cybersecurity threshold, so it shipped with safeguards that refuse advanced cyber tasks such as proof-of-concept exploits.

events.title: GPT-6 rolls out in ChatGPT
events.note: OpenAI began rolling GPT-6 out across ChatGPT, including the free tier, and added Intelligent UI, which can answer with charts, forms and small interactive tools as well as text.
